title: Generic Type Inference
concept: The compiler can often infer type parameters from the arguments you pass — so you don't need to write them explicitly.
why: Explicit type parameters add noise: `first[Int](&nums)`. Inference makes generics feel natural: `first(&nums)`. Less typing, same safety.
tips: Let the compiler infer types — it's almost always right and saves keystrokes
Add explicit type params when the inferred type is surprising — it documents intent
If the compiler asks for explicit types, add them — it means inference is ambiguous
Use type annotations on variables (let x: Type = ...) to guide inference
common_mistakes: Adding explicit type params everywhere — defeats the purpose of inference
Assuming inference always works — it needs enough context from arguments
Writing turbofish style `::<Type>` — XIOM uses square brackets: `func[Type]`
